name: autokey encrypt, primer QUEENLY
ref: Wikipedia "Autokey cipher" worked example (primer QUEENLY, attackatdawn -> QNXEPVYTWTWP)

example.title: Lower case in, lower case out
example.note: Lower-case input gives lower-case output, with the same primer key.

name: autokey encrypt, upper case
ref: Wikipedia "Autokey cipher" worked example (primer QUEENLY, attackatdawn -> QNXEPVYTWTWP)

example.title: The primer, then the message
example.note: The primer QUEENLY is the start of the key, and each later key letter is a letter of the message, so the output starts QNXEP.

name: autokey decrypt, primer QUEENLY
ref: Wikipedia "Autokey cipher" worked example (primer QUEENLY, attackatdawn -> QNXEPVYTWTWP)

example.title: Each recovered letter joins the key
example.note: Each plaintext letter joins the key as it is found, so QNXEPVYTWTWP gives back ATTACKATDAWN from the primer QUEENLY.

name: Gronsfeld encrypt, digits 31415
ref: Gronsfeld: the Vigenere-style definition with digit shifts, hand-computed and checked by a Python script

example.title: Digits as the key
example.note: Each digit shifts the letter in its place, so A moved by 3 gives D, and the output is Duxbhn bx efzo.

name: Gronsfeld decrypt, digits 31415
ref: Gronsfeld: the Vigenere-style definition with digit shifts, hand-computed and checked by a Python script

example.title: Undo the digit shifts
example.note: With the key 31415 the shifts are taken back, so Duxbhn bx efzo reads Attack at dawn again.

name: Gronsfeld with a single digit is a Caesar shift
ref: Gronsfeld: the Vigenere-style definition with digit shifts, hand-computed and checked by a Python script

example.title: A single digit is a Caesar shift
example.note: With the key 3 every letter moves by 3, and the space passes through without using a digit.

name: Beaufort, key LEMON
ref: Beaufort: the standard definition C = (K - P) mod 26, hand-computed and checked by a Python script

example.title: Subtract the key letter
example.note: Each letter is the key letter minus the message letter, modulo 26, so A under L gives L and the output is LLTOLBETLNPR.

example.title: The same word gives the message back
example.note: Beaufort is its own inverse: the output above goes back through the same key to ATTACKATDAWN.
